truth_states: FACT = verified in source at the cited line; UPSTREAM = bundled-doc claim, drift-prone; INFERENCE = producer reasoning, labeled

entries.name: Tool-calling capability gate for direct/pinned requests
entries.purpose: checkToolCallingRequiredButUnsupported blocks a direct (non-combo) request carrying a non-empty tools[] array when the resolved model's unsupported list includes 'tools', returning an explicit error instead of silently stripping tools and producing a 200 that can never call anything (live incident cited in module header: AI Horde/Behemoth-X-123B narrating fake actions).
entries.risk_class: medium — fail-closed gate on agentic traffic; a false positive blocks legitimate tool requests, a false negative silently degrades them
dependencies: model capability resolution (getResolvedModelCapabilities via comboStructure.ts filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility, per module header comment)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — direct request with tools[] to a tool-incapable model must return the explicit block error, not a 200; negative — combo requests must NOT be blocked here (isCombo short-circuit at toolCallingRequiredCheck.ts:25); direct — empty tools[] must pass
entries.rollback_or_disable: Gate is inherent to the chat path; removal is source-level (delete the chatCore.ts:2738 check). No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Request tool-definition normalization (mixed shapes → OpenAI function form)
entries.purpose: normalizeOpenAICompatibleTools converts heterogeneous incoming tool shapes (bare name/input_schema, Responses custom tools) into {type:'function', function:{...}} while passing Responses-API formats through untouched and counting dropped entries; defaultClaudeToolType defaults a missing Claude tool `type` to 'custom' to avoid upstream HTTP 400.
entries.risk_class: medium — mis-normalization silently drops or mangles client tool declarations before translation
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — mixed-shape tools array round-trips to canonical function form with correct dropped count; routed — Responses-format requests must pass through unmodified; negative — Claude tools without type must gain type:'custom'
entries.rollback_or_disable: Pure transform; removal is source-level. No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Tool-name identity ledger (normalize → alias → restore)
entries.purpose: normalizeOpenAIToolNames rewrites over-long/invalid function names to provider-safe aliases and returns an alias ledger; restoreOpenAIToolNames / restoreClaudePassthroughToolNames / restoreNonStreamingToolNames map upstream tool-call names back to client-declared names (including the Claude OAuth prefix map and the executor _toolNameMap side channel merged at passthroughToolNames.ts:53); extractRequestToolIdentityMap recovers the #7936/#9780 namespace identity ledger from translated bodies; restoreClaudePassthroughToolUseName does the same inside the streaming SSE transform.
entries.risk_class: medium — a lost ledger returns aliased tool names to the client, breaking agent-loop tool dispatch (wrong-tool execution)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — alias/restore round-trip for over-long and prefixed names; routed — streaming Claude passthrough restores tool_use block names (stream.ts:592); negative — case-insensitive lookup must not cross-map distinct tools (toolCallHelper.ts:109)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Passing a null map disables restoration (names pass through as upstream sent them); no runtime toggle found

entries.name: Tool-call id and tool-result repair helpers
entries.purpose: ensureToolCallIds generates/normalizes missing or non-conformant tool_call ids (optional 9-char [a-zA-Z0-9] mode for Mistral-class upstreams); fixMissingToolResponses synthesizes placeholder tool results for tool_calls that lack one; stripOrphanedToolResults drops tool results whose call id no longer exists — keeping request history structurally valid for strict upstreams.
entries.risk_class: medium — synthesized placeholder results alter conversation semantics; over-aggressive orphan stripping drops real history
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — history with missing ids/results is repaired to schema-valid form; negative — valid history must pass through unchanged; routed — strict upstream (e.g. Mistral 9-char ids) accepts repaired payload
entries.rollback_or_disable: Helpers are opt-in call sites in translators/executors; removal is source-level. No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Streamed tool-call argument fragment accumulation
entries.purpose: appendToolCallArgumentDelta accumulates streamed tool-call arguments, concatenating incremental deltas verbatim while deduplicating only unambiguous full-snapshot repeats (#3701), and JSON-stringifying non-conformant object-shaped argument fragments instead of dropping them (#6459); the module explicitly rejects fuzzy overlap heuristics that silently truncate legitimate deltas.
entries.risk_class: high — argument corruption produces wrong-parameter tool execution downstream; the module documents prior silent-truncation and '[object Object]' failure modes
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — delta/snapshot/object fragment fixtures assert byte-exact assembly; negative — repeated leading bytes ('ls -ll') must survive; regression — issue #3701 duplication and #6459 object-fragment cases
entries.rollback_or_disable: Pure function used at assembly call sites; removal is source-level

entries.name: Text-protocol tool-call parsing (non-JSON tool-call emissions)
entries.purpose: parseTextualToolCallCandidate recovers tool calls emitted as plain text ('[Tool call: name]\nArguments: {json}') with zero-width-character stripping and partial/complete classification for streaming; composerToolCalls.ts parses Cursor Composer's DeepSeek-style inline sentinel format (<|tool_calls_begin|> ...) from normal text output.
entries.risk_class: medium — false-positive parsing converts ordinary prose into a tool call; false negatives leak raw protocol text to the client
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — complete/partial/negative fixtures incl. zero-width obfuscation; routed — Composer-format upstream stream yields structured tool_calls; negative — prose containing '[Tool call:' without Arguments: must not misfire (containsTextualToolCallMarker gate)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Parser invocation is per-path in the transform; removal is source-level. No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Per-tool argument shims (TOOL_SHIMS registry)
entries.purpose: TOOL_SHIMS is a registry of per-tool-name defensive argument transformers applied to assembled OpenAI tool-call arguments before re-emission as a single Claude input_json_delta — e.g. the Read shim clamps limit to <=2000 (Claude Code cap), coerces stringified numbers, drops negative offsets and invalid PDF pages args that cause client retry loops.
entries.risk_class: medium — shim bugs rewrite legitimate tool arguments; the registry pattern invites unreviewed per-tool exceptions
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — oversized limit/negative offset/string number fixtures are clamped/coerced; negative — unregistered tool names pass through untouched; routed — cleaned args reach Claude Code client without retry loop
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the tool-name entry from TOOL_SHIMS (toolCallShim.ts:71) — arguments then pass through unmodified

entries.name: Tool-schema sanitization for strict upstream validators
entries.purpose: sanitizeAntigravityToolPayload recursively strips enumDescriptions from Antigravity tool schemas (upstream rejects the field with HTTP 400) while preserving tool identity/order; toolSchemaSanitizer.ts strips null entries from enum schemas for strict JSON-Schema validators (Moonshot via opencode-go/kimi-k2.6, per module header).
entries.risk_class: medium — schema rewriting can drop validation constraints the client relied on; failures surface as upstream 400s
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — enumDescriptions removed from anyOf/allOf/$defs nests; routed — sanitized payload accepted by strict-validator mock; negative — tool names/order/identity must be unchanged
entries.rollback_or_disable: Sanitizers are call-site applied; removal is source-level. The earlier decoy-injection cloaking mechanism was already removed upstream (see CAP-P3-026)

entries.name: Tool-history flattening for prose-only legs
entries.purpose: flattenToolHistory converts structured tool turns (OpenAI tool/function roles + tool_calls, Anthropic tool_use/tool_result blocks) into plain assistant prose when a combo leg or fan-out strips tool definitions — preventing agentic models from emitting tool_calls with no tools declared (which produced empty prose and upstream 503s, per module header).
entries.risk_class: medium — lossy history rewrite; over-flattening erases tool context the model needed
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — OpenAI and Anthropic tool-turn fixtures flatten to prose; routed — stripped-tools combo leg no longer triggers empty-prose 503; negative — requests keeping tools must not be flattened
entries.rollback_or_disable: Applied only on the strip path; removal is source-level

entries.name: Structured-output (response_format) translation and downgrade
entries.purpose: response_format is mapped per target: injected as a system-prompt JSON instruction for Claude (no native support, openai-to-claude.ts:468-472 comment); converted to responseMimeType/responseSchema for Gemini; mapped to json_schema/json_object or text.format for Responses-API targets (translator/index.ts:123 normalization); DefaultExecutor downgrades json_schema→json_object or strips response_format entirely for providers that reject it (kilocode DeepSeek 400, default.ts:623-682); tool_choice is similarly translated Chat→Responses at toResponses.ts:359.
entries.risk_class: medium — structured-output semantics degrade silently on the Claude prompt-injection path (schema adherence becomes model-dependent); over-stripping loses machine-checkable output
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — json_schema request round-trips per target format; negative — provider rejecting response_format must receive the downgraded/stripped form, never the raw field; direct — tool_choice object→{type:function,name} mapping
entries.rollback_or_disable: Translation pairs unregister via translator/bootstrap.ts; downgrade rules are data/code in DefaultExecutor — source-level revert

entries.name: Tool-policy allowlist/denylist (TOOL_POLICY_MODE)
entries.purpose: Env-driven (TOOL_POLICY_MODE=allowlist|denylist|disabled, default disabled) tool-name invocation policy with runtime override via setRuntimePolicy, intended to prevent dangerous tool use via prompt injection — BUT: deterministic grep for validateToolsInRequest / evaluateToolPolicy / toolPolicy imports across the corpus finds zero call sites outside the module itself [FACT]; the policy engine exists but is not wired into any request path.
entries.risk_class: medium — a security-relevant control that appears available but is inert gives false assurance; wiring it changes traffic behavior (denied tools)
dependencies: no runtime dependencies; would need a call site in the chat request path (chatCore.ts) to function
entries.test_contract: Layer-N (if ever wired): routed — denylisted tool name in tools[]/tool_choice must be rejected before dispatch; negative — disabled mode must pass everything; direct — extractToolNames covers tools/functions/tool_choice shapes (toolPolicy.ts:115)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Already inert (no call site); TOOL_POLICY_MODE defaults to disabled; resetRuntimePolicy clears runtime overrides (toolPolicy.ts:65)

entries.name: Unified SSE transform (createSSEStream)
entries.purpose: The core SSE TransformStream: TRANSLATE mode (format-to-format chunk conversion) and PASSTHROUGH mode (normalize + usage extraction), idle-timeout protection (STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS), canonical TTFT/ITL timing (createStreamTiming, marked on first forwarded chunk), per-client-format [DONE] suppression (Claude/Antigravity SDKs break on a trailing [DONE], stream.ts:697-716 comments), and Responses commentary dropping (#6199 feature-flagged).
entries.risk_class: high — every streamed chat response flows through this transform; a defect corrupts or truncates all SSE traffic
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — golden SSE fixtures per format pair incl. [DONE] presence/absence per client format; negative — idle upstream must trip the timeout error, not hang; direct — TTFT marked on first forwarded chunk
entries.rollback_or_disable: Inherent to the streaming path; no kill-switch found. Revert is source-level

entries.name: Streaming response pipeline assembly (disconnect → PII → progress → heartbeat → model-echo)
entries.purpose: assembleStreamingPipeline chains the post-transform stream stages in fixed order: disconnect-aware pipe → optional PII sanitization (explicit transform or PII_RESPONSE_SANITIZATION flag) → opt-in progress tracking → SSE heartbeat keepalive (default 15s, comment/Anthropic-ping/OpenAI-chunk shapes, OMNIROUTE_SSE_COMMENTS gate) → optional model-echo (#1311 alias name in each chunk).
entries.risk_class: medium — transform-order or heartbeat-shape mistakes break specific client SDKs (the module documents such incidents); PII stage touches response content
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — heartbeat frames arrive within interval on a stalled upstream; negative — comment-shaped heartbeats must not reach SDK clients when OMNIROUTE_SSE_COMMENTS=off; direct — transform order assertion (pipe → pii → progress → heartbeat → echo)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Progress/PII/echo stages are individually opt-in/flag-gated; heartbeat interval configurable; core pipe is inherent

entries.name: Stream cancellation and client-disconnect handling
entries.purpose: createStreamController owns an AbortController bridged to the client request signal (deadline-abort reasons distinguished from true client disconnects, streamHandler.ts:190/426); isClientDisconnectError classifies AbortError/ResponseAborted so cancelled requests skip the failover/cooldown path (one cancelled request must not mark a provider bad); createClientDisconnectGraceHandler (#9653) polls for completion before recording a 499 so a disconnect-after-full-delivery is not mis-logged; pipeline errors map to 499 client_disconnected vs 502 stream error; wrapReadableStreamWithFinalize runs a finalize callback exactly once on drain/error/cancel.
entries.risk_class: high — mis-classified disconnects either poison provider health state (failover storms) or leak hung upstream connections
dependencies: client request AbortSignal from the route layer
resilience/cooldown services (P1/P6 scope — interaction point only)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — client abort mid-stream aborts the upstream fetch and records 499 client_disconnected with zero usage; negative — client abort must NOT trip provider cooldown; regression — #9653 disconnect-after-complete records success, not 499
entries.rollback_or_disable: Grace period configurable (gracePeriodMs <= 0 restores pre-#9653 immediate finalize); core abort plumbing is inherent

entries.name: Stream failure finalization and per-format error framing
entries.purpose: createStreamFailureFinalizers records failed streams once (buildErrorBody payload, persistFailureUsage, failure callback); normalizeStreamFailurePayload extracts status/code/message from heterogeneous upstream error bodies (429 heuristic for rate-limit wording, else 502); formatTranslatedStreamError emits the error in the client's SSE dialect (response.failed for Responses API, event:error for Claude, data+ [DONE] for OpenAI); shouldPassthroughUpstreamError relays upstream 4xx bodies verbatim for Claude Code's capability auto-recovery contract — but refuses passthrough on 401/403/407, internal-path leaks, or credential-pattern echoes (CREDENTIAL_LEAK_RE, #10898-sec).
entries.risk_class: high — verbatim error passthrough is a credential-leak vector (mitigated by regex refusal); wrong status mapping defeats client retry semantics
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — upstream 4xx with capability wording relays verbatim; negative — body containing Bearer/sk- patterns must fall back to sanitized buildErrorBody; direct — status extraction order and 429 heuristic; per-format error-frame shape goldens
entries.rollback_or_disable: Passthrough is a decision function — returning false restores sanitized errors everywhere; finalizers are inherent to the stream path

entries.name: Finish-reason normalization and abort classification
entries.purpose: normalizeOpenAICompatibleFinishReason canonicalizes provider finish reasons (max_tokens→length, safety family→content_filter) while deliberately NOT collapsing abort reasons (malformed_function_call, unexpected_tool_call) to a misleading 'stop' — the Claude translation classifies them via isAbortFinishReason so an aborted tool call cannot present as a clean end_turn (9router#2462); isMalformedToolCallFinishReason lets gemini-to-openai synthesize a tool_calls entry + finish_reason:'tool_calls' instead (OpenClaw incident 1784489701456-d8c0e9); normalizeOpenAIToolFinishReasons forces finish_reason:'tool_calls' on non-streaming responses carrying tool_calls.
entries.risk_class: medium — wrong finish mapping makes agent loops misread terminal state (infinite retries or silently dropped failures, both documented in source comments)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — reason-mapping table fixtures (stop/length/tool_calls/content_filter/max_tokens/safety family); negative — abort reasons must NOT map to stop/end_turn; routed — malformed_function_call stream surfaces as tool_calls failure to an OpenAI client
entries.rollback_or_disable: Mapping tables are data; revert is source-level. No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Empty-stream rejection guard (#9268)
entries.purpose: A streaming provider that completes having forwarded only empty choices:[] chunks (no content, tool_calls, or finish_reason) is rejected instead of terminating as a clean empty 200 — the SSE transform threads a forwardedValuableChunk boolean so clients get an error to stop on rather than retrying an apparently-valid empty turn to their cap.
entries.risk_class: medium — false positive rejects legitimately empty responses; absence caused client retry storms (documented #9268)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — all-empty-choices upstream stream yields an error frame, not a 200 empty turn; negative — any forwarded valuable chunk must suppress the guard
entries.rollback_or_disable: Guard is a boolean decision in the transform path; removal is source-level. No runtime toggle found

entries.name: Stream-recovery holdback (truncated-stream transparent retry)
entries.purpose: Opt-in (ResilienceSettings.streamRecovery, default OFF) holdback window that retries an upstream stream truncated before any byte reached the client, invisibly to the client; ported from free-claude-code's always-on recovery but kept off by default because the holdback adds up to HOLDBACK_MS of TTFT on every streaming request (module header).
entries.risk_class: medium — transparent retry replays non-idempotent upstream calls; the TTFT cost is why it ships disabled
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — pre-first-byte truncation retries once transparently; negative — post-first-byte truncation must NOT retry (client already has partial data); direct — default-off assertion from settings resolution
entries.rollback_or_disable: Disabled by default; per-settings toggle off is the disable path

entries.name: Early stream keepalive
entries.purpose: Emits keepalive bytes/frames before the upstream produces its first output (bridge the pre-TTFT gap so proxies/clients do not time out the connection), distinct from the mid-stream heartbeat in CAP-P3-013.
entries.risk_class: low — keepalive bytes must match the client's SSE dialect; a wrong shape breaks parsers (same class as heartbeat-shape incidents)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — slow upstream (delay > keepalive interval) still yields pre-TTFT frames the client accepts; negative — keepalive must stop once real chunks flow
entries.rollback_or_disable: Keepalive stage is pipeline-attached; interval/disable via the same heartbeat/keepalive configuration surface [INFERENCE: exact toggle line not traced this partition]

entries.purpose: Two independent stream-lifecycle trackers exist: StreamTracker state machine (INITIALIZED→CONNECTING→STREAMING→COMPLETED|FAILED|CANCELLED with a valid-transition table and an active-stream registry, streamState.ts:179) and a metrics tracker (token counts, TTFT, tokens/sec progress callbacks). Deterministic grep finds NO production import of either — streamState.ts is referenced only by tests/unit/advanced-fase07-09.test.ts; shared/utils/streamTracker.ts only by a doc-check script comment [FACT — import grep corpus-wide].

entries.name: Usage extraction (streaming and non-streaming, multi-format)
entries.purpose: extractUsage pulls token usage from streaming chunks across Claude (message_start/message_delta, folding cache_read+cache_creation into prompt tokens, FIX #74), OpenAI Responses (response.completed), and Gemini shapes; extractUsageFromResponse does the same for non-streaming bodies across OpenAI (incl. DeepSeek flat cache fields, xAI cost_in_usd_ticks passthrough), Claude (input+cache sum), Responses, and Gemini usageMetadata (thoughts folded into completion, antigravity envelope unwrap #59d858b); normalizeUsage canonicalizes field names.
entries.risk_class: medium — under-counted usage breaks quota/billing accuracy; the code documents multiple provider-specific counting fixes
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — per-format usage fixtures (OpenAI/Claude/Responses/Gemini, cache and reasoning fields); negative — missing usage block yields null, not zeros; regression — cache-fold and thoughts-fold arithmetic
entries.rollback_or_disable: Pure extraction; revert is source-level

entries.name: Client-visible usage buffering, filtering, and estimation
entries.purpose: applyClientUsageBuffer post-processes response usage for the client: post-#8331 the safety buffer stays OUT of client-visible metering fields (billing reflects real upstream usage) except the Claude-Code-compatible path where context_budget_* fields fold back into visible prompt/input/total fields; empty or all-zero provider usage (common for web providers) triggers content-length estimation (estimateUsage); filterUsageForFormat renames fields per client format.
entries.risk_class: medium — the buffer exists to prevent CLI context-window errors; mis-scoping it inflates billing or starves CLI headroom (the #8331 regression class)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — buffer excluded from visible fields for API clients, folded back for claude-code-compatible; routed — zero-usage web-provider response yields an estimate, not a constant 2000; negative — isEmptyUsage must not misfire on real small usages
entries.rollback_or_disable: Buffer size configurable (USAGE_TOKEN_BUFFER); scoping logic revert is source-level

entries.name: Usage persistence, dedup, failure and rejection accounting
entries.purpose: saveRequestUsage inserts per-request rows into SQLite usage_history (UsageEntry contract, usageHistory.ts:614) with a same-second natural-key dedup guard preventing double-count when success callbacks fire twice; trackPendingRequest/finalizePendingRequest manage in-flight request lifecycle; streaming/non-streaming paths record fire-and-forget rows plus per-api-key billable-token counters (recordTokenUsage, 200-only for streams); buildFailureUsageRecord zeroes tokens with success:false for failed requests; recordRejectedRequestUsage writes BOTH call_logs and usage_history for pre-dispatch gate rejections so per-key counters include rejected traffic (2026-07-08 support-mesh escalation); streamingCost/streamingQuotaShare attach cost and shared-quota consumption on stream completion.
entries.risk_class: high — this is the metering/billing source of truth; double-counts or dropped rejections corrupt quota enforcement and cost reporting
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: persistence — success/failure/rejection rows land in usage_history with correct success/status/tokens and survive restart; negative — duplicate same-second callback must not double-insert; direct — billable counter fires only on 200 streams
entries.rollback_or_disable: Persistence is best-effort (writes swallow own errors) and gated by shouldPersistToDisk (usageHistory.ts:642); DB backup/restore per P5 runbooks
